summary: This bill renames the Salem Maritime National Historic Site as the Salem Maritime National Historical Park and requires the Interior Secretary to study whether to add nearby Salem sites tied to maritime history, coastal defenses, and military activity, then report findings to Congress within three years.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a boundary study for potential expansion of a national historical park. This requires the allocation of federal funds to perform the study and prepare a report to Congress. While the fiscal impact is small and administrative in nature, the legislation does authorize new government activity that entails modest additional spending rather than any reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses only the redesignation and boundary study of a historical park; it has no connection to healthcare policy or systems.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation deals exclusively with a national park redesignation and study; it does not address immigration, borders, or related protections.
The bill has no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.

Although the boundary study includes evaluation of sites related to military history and coastal defenses, the bill does not authorize, fund, or alter any military or defense spending or programs; it is limited to National Park System planning.
The bill focuses on historical designation and study; it contains no environmental regulatory changes or climate-related provisions.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other social safety-net policies.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The legislation has no bearing on sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains nothing related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
Any spending implications are minimal and indirect; the bill does not engage with deficit policy or debt reduction strategies.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill does not mention or affect foreign aid programs.
No election-related or voting-access provisions are present.
The legislation has no technology, data, or privacy regulatory content.
Nothing in the bill pertains to worker protections, unions, or employment policy.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
